Acceptance run: 1 of 6 'yes' (Priya, Solo $39), 5 of 6 'maybe' (Olena Salon $79, Jessica Pro $149 + sync, Marc Salon $79 + Booksy sync, Anna Pro $149 + sync, conversion critic), 0 'no'. About 70% of owners now reach Go live in 12-30 min (run 1: 20-45 min). Every 'maybe' names the same conditions: a working calendar sync or owner calendar, an alert when a client writes after a handoff, and paying on the spot.
verdict.summary: Big step up. The three things that killed the sale in run 1 are fixed or mostly fixed: the landing now sells the product, prices are visible everywhere, and Maya answers in the client's language and respects staff days, services and hours when she books. Buy intent went from 0/6 to 1 yes and 5 maybe. Fully fixed: #4 price guard, #6 landing, #15 names, #18 Go live, #24 walk-ins/closing time. Most others are partly fixed. Still broken: #17 (the preview locks after a handoff; 4 of 5 owners hit it, see olena-nails/31-prev-en-3.png, where the notice is in Russian inside an English test) and #23 (two brands). New top blocker: after a handoff, a Telegram client's next messages get no reply and the owner gets no alert. Anna, Priya, Marc, Jessica and the critic all hit it; Anna rated it a blocker. Next: there is no owner calendar or way to block busy time, and test bookings take real slots and count as revenue. Payment is still an emailed invoice. The dashboard is still the Luminous Core demo (anna-medspa/60-dashboard.png: 'Sarah J. Manager', 'Friday, Apr 17', '+9.4% vs last month', broken avatars). Fix: send the client a holding notice in their language and alert the owner on each new inbound message (throttled), or hand back to Maya automatically after N minutes.

The owner cannot see or protect her calendar (critic: blocker; #1 reason for Jessica and Marc; Priya and Olena too): there is no bookings or week view linked from the app and no busy-time blocking, and preview test bookings hold real slots and count as revenue. Calendar sync is a +$29 add-on connected by hand, not in the trial, with no Jane App. So owners won't share the link with real clients, and the trial shows no value.

7. Text the owner typed is sent untranslated: policy, staff and service names reach clients in the owner's language, and French clients see English service names (a problem for Quebec).

#7 Confirmation loop: a server-side booking draft (session.state.draft: service, day, time, staff, offeredDays) plus session.state.client (name, phone). An affirmative after a read-back (yes/yeah/ok/sure/da/да/так/oui/ouais/c'est bon/parfait/d'accord...) commits the staged action in code BEFORE the LLM runs, with no model call. If the yes carries a question, the booking is committed first, then the model answers only that question (booking tools removed for that call); if the model gives no answer, the question goes to the owner with an honest line. 'yes but Saturday', 'oui mais plutôt...', 'Correct?' and 'Верно ли...?' never commit. An ambiguous service is settled by the client's answer or the draft, so 'coupe simple ou coupe + barbe?' is not asked again. A self-composed 'Vous confirmez?/Shall I book it?' with no tool call is staged from the draft and replaced by the official read-back (or a name question). A read-back that does not show the time is replaced by the official one, and repeating the same message twice falls back to the read-back.

#8 Dates: new backend/maya-dates.js resolves today/tomorrow/après-demain/послезавтра, weekdays with next/prochain/следующий, month names in en/fr/ru/uk, ISO dates, a year the model guessed wrong ('2024-09-24' becomes the nearest future date), 'in 3 days/dans 3 jours/через 3 дня' and unambiguous dd/mm. A date in the past returns date_in_past with today's date. Offsets are now taken from the store's day_anchor, which fixes an off-by-one where last_updated was stale. Every turn gets a TODAY block with the year, salon time and a 14-day date/weekday/hours table, plus the client's own date words resolved. Tool results carry ISO 'date'. A booking-day drift guard pulls a book_appointment day that was neither named nor offered back to the day already settled (a live run showed 'next Thursday' drifting to Tuesday).
